hook: At matched memory and nominal bit-width, candidate-order agreement should improve more by protecting sites with high rollout-ranking influence than by protecting sites with the largest local reconstruction error, especially in the longer-horizon cells of the evaluation grid. falsification_prediction: Minimal experiment: on one public FP16 DreamerV3- or TD-MPC2-style checkpoint (inferred pilot anchor) and one DeepMind Control Suite visual continuous-control task, compare RankCal with uniform-bit and local-reconstruction allocation at matched peak memory across the full C grid. If the mechanism works, the primary downstream metric, closed-loop task-success rate, will be higher for RankCal than for the matched controls, while candidate-order and first-action agreement will degrade less in the longer-horizon cells. The single load-bearing variable is I_g(b), the site-only rollout-ranking influence profile; randomize its mapping to bit pairs while preserving the bit histogram, memory, candidate/update schedule, receding-horizon convention, and tie rule, then rerun fresh D_eval episodes. The negative control predicts that the randomized map's downstream task-success rate returns to the matched local-reconstruction or uniform-PTQ baseline, not merely that I_g changes; if the benefit survives the randomized mapping, the proposed influence signal is not the mechanism carrying the result.
compute_budget: GPU: estimated 12 GPU-days on one NSCC ASPIRE2A A100-SXM4-40GB for the one-task pilot, site-only probes, full nuisance grid, matched controls, and held-out closed-loop evaluation; an optional second DMC task family would add an estimated 6 GPU-days. API: $0 for the full campaign because model inference, calibration, and evaluation are local and no paid API judge is required. No GPU experiments are run during this proposal phase.
what_step_was_missed: It would have needed to hold candidate pools, planner inputs, receding-horizon conventions, and tie rules fixed while quantizing one site at a time, estimate that site's candidate-order discordance over action-conditioned rollout states, and solve the resulting profile as a memory-constrained mixed W/A assignment; the supplied method constructs PTQ sweeps and outcome analyses but not this decision-influence object or allocation step.

differentiation_from_lit.delta: The full-text-backed DINO-WM record constructs a systematic weight-only and joint weight-activation PTQ sweep over methods, granularity, modules, and planning horizons, whereas RankCal constructs a site-level counterfactual candidate-order influence profile over action-conditioned latent states and uses it for memory-constrained mixed W/A assignment.

The full-text-backed LeFlow record replaces repeated CEM search with rectified-flow latent trajectory generation, inverse-dynamics decoding, and frozen-LeWM rollout reranking, whereas RankCal leaves the planner and latent backbone fixed and changes the numerical PTQ calibration/allocation signal to preserve candidate ordering under multi-step quantized rollouts.

The connector-verified but abstract-only adjacent QuantWAMs record proposes coordinate-compatible activation evidence, joint video-action saliency, and fixed-intervention auditing for WAM PTQ, whereas RankCal targets latent-dynamics planner rankings without WAM future/action coupling and derives weight/activation bits from site-only ranking influence.

The official-HTML full-text record for the user-supplied pure ID 2602.11882, Where Bits Matter in World-Model Planning: A Paired Mixed-Bit Study for Efficient Spatial Reasoning, compares paired mixed-bit/planner-budget allocations by DINO-WM planning success, whereas RankCal uses a frozen action-conditioned latent-dynamics, site-only candidate-order influence estimand, a measured system-level PeakBytes constraint, and an exact histogram-plus-bytes permutation. This is latent world-model planning rather than a WAM future/action-denoising prior; QuantWAMs remains the connector-verified but abstract-only adjacent WAM record.

reviewer_concerns_and_responses.attack: Paper-pointed threat: arxiv:2602.02110v1 (lit_table). arxiv:2602.02110v1 is the strongest run-pool threat: lit_table marks it host_recall, and the candidate identifies connector-verified H/html_arxiv full text; it already varies weight-only and joint W/A PTQ by module, granularity, and horizon and reports planning-objective/task-success mismatch. The supplemental review also supplies the exact identity and title arxiv:2602.11882v1, Where Bits Matter in World-Model Planning, with official-HTML sections 4–6 evidence of paired mixed-bit/planner-budget comparisons and planning-success allocation, so it is not dropped because of a failed title lookup; it also records arxiv:2607.28405v1 as connector-verified host_recall, while this run's candidate evidence is abstract-only with no fulltext cache entry (the supplemental review separately reports official-HTML section/equation checks). These priors threaten the broad decision-aware and mixed-precision framing, but the supplied evidence does not show the same imagined action-sequence latent-dynamics branch, frozen-model all-other-FP16 site-only candidate-order estimand, measured end-to-end PeakBytes-constrained mixed W/A assignment, or exact histogram-plus-bytes permutation; QuantWAMs remains a WAM joint future/action-denoising prior, not an exact branch match. The threat is therefore addressable differentiation, not exact-mechanism overlap or novelty certification.
